manager_rule: Track a persistent 'stale_targeting_consecutive_rounds' counter: after any round where stub_compiler_stale_targeting fires (a /SENSEC{N}_HI or /SENSEC{N}_LO net is in failing_reasons but absent from the compiler's nets list), increment the counter; reset it to zero only in a round where the compiler's nets list contains at least one /SENSEC{N}_HI or /SENSEC{N}_LO entry for every cable N present in failing_reasons. When this counter reaches 5 without a reset, HALT all FR dispatch and log 'persistent_stale_targeting_halt' with fields: (a) the counter value, (b) the list of rounds in which stale targeting fired, (c) the compiler nets list and failing_reasons for each such round, and (d) the current stub compiler's full priority/decay weight table. Human clearance requires: (1) a code change that rebuilds the compiler's entire net-priority state from scratch using ONLY the most recent round's failing_reasons as input, discarding all accumulated historical weights, (2) a test demonstrating that after this reset the compiler's nets list for a synthetic board state with /SENSEC1_HI and /SENSEC1_LO in failing_reasons contains at least one of those two net names, and (3) explicit written authorization to resume. The rationale: a per-round same-round correction (existing Rule 23) adjusts the current dispatch but cannot fix a priority model that has chronically mis-ranked Kelvin nets across many rounds; five consecutive stale rounds is evidence the priority model itself is miscalibrated beyond what incremental corrections can repair, and continuing to dispatch FR with a broken priority model wastes compute budget with no convergence path.
